S01: In an old European city, beneath the cobblestones, stood a small grocery shop.
S02: Inside, among the shelves of goods, it was warm and smelled of spices.
S03: There, in a chest, lived the tiny elf.
S04: And every day the good grocer brought him a dish of rice with butter.
S05: It was a truly tasty meal!
S07: Thus the two lived — in peace and quiet.
S08: One evening the door opened and a student entered.
S09: Student: "Good evening. A piece of cheese, please."
S10: But the student noticed that the grocer was wrapping the cheese in pages torn from an old book.
S11: Student: "What are you doing with that book? Allow me... let me buy the whole thing."
S12: Grocer: "Of course! I don't need it anyway."
S13: The boy laughed: "I'm sure you don't need it."
S14: And the elf grew angry — he thought the student was being insolent to his protector.
S15: And so, he resolved to follow him, to play a trick on him.
S16: He followed him quietly through the streets.
S17: All the way to his humble room.
S18: The student drew out the torn book and opened it.
S19: Then, from the pages came a ray of light.
S20: Student: "What is this...?", he whispered in wonder.
S21: The light grew, accompanied by melodious music.
S22: And the ray slowly became a tree.
S23: A tree on which hung flowers and fruits.
S26: The student gazed at the marvel.
S27: And from the shadows, the elf watched in amazement.
S28: The whole room turned into an enchanted garden.
S29: The elf drew nearer, unable to resist.
S30: Every flower glowed like a tiny star.
S31: Elf: "I want to stay here forever..."
S32: Elf: "...but the boy doesn't give me rice and butter!"
S33: But the tree shone more beautifully than anything."
S34: The music spilled through the room.
S35: Elf: "Still, I will come one more time..."
S36: And so, in the morning he returned home.
S37: The grocer, as every day, prepared him a dish of rice with butter.
S38: Elf: "Thank you, grocer. I cannot live without this food."
S39: But from that day, every evening he returned to the student.
S40: He could not live without the grocer's food, but the beautiful book was a greater treasure.
S41: Every evening he awaited the tree of light.
S42: And with it, the little elf — happy.
S43: For some treasures cannot be eaten — but they feed the heart.
